note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Sparse verbalized confidence, its evaluation consequences, and the verbalization-logprobs fix

nodes.name: LLMs prefer certain number tokens
nodes.description: LLMs strongly prefer generating certain numerical tokens, which biases verbalized confidence estimates.

nodes.name: Verbalized confidences are extremely sparse
nodes.description: Vanilla verbalization yields very few unique confidence values; Qwen3-32B predicts only eight on SST-2 with over half equal to 95%, and 45-93% of confidences fall in the five most common values across four datasets.

nodes.name: Sparsity limits threshold choice
nodes.description: Sparse confidences leave little choice of decision threshold: reaching at least 98% accuracy on SST-2 requires rejecting 39.7% of predictions versus 23.6% for 97.9% accuracy.

nodes.name: Stepwise interpolation is correct for sparse scores
nodes.description: With sparse confidences the correct way to compute AUARC is stepwise interpolation; linear (trapezoidal) interpolation wrongly assumes gradual change between thresholds and inflates scores.

nodes.name: Interpolation inflates sparse methods
nodes.description: Verbalization and sampling approaches score 0.7-4.5 AUARC points lower under stepwise than linear interpolation, while continuous token logprobs are unaffected.

nodes.name: Interpolation changes rankings
nodes.description: Consistency sampling ranks first under linear interpolation but last under stepwise interpolation, a 12.5-point absolute decrease.

nodes.name: Verbalization logprobs method
nodes.description: Verbalization logprobs computes confidence as the expected value over verbalized digits weighted by their token probabilities, turning sparse verbalized values into continuous estimates.

nodes.name: Verbalization logprobs removes sparsity
nodes.description: Verbalization logprobs uses at least 630 unique values (up to 2,227 on ESCI), an 80x-200x resolution increase, and cuts top-5 concentration from 92% to 1%.

nodes.name: Finer thresholds salvage data
nodes.description: With verbalization logprobs, 98% accuracy requires rejecting only 28.1% of examples instead of 39.7%, salvaging 11.6% of data.

nodes.name: Verbalization logprobs improves metrics
nodes.description: Verbalization logprobs improves on vanilla verbalization by +2.3 AUARC and +0.9 AUROC and on token logprobs by +1.3 AUARC and +4.7 AUROC at no added computational cost.

nodes.name: Matches sampling at lower cost
nodes.description: Verbalization logprobs matches verbalization sampling, the strongest baseline, in AUARC (0.736 vs 0.734) at 1.7x cost instead of 6.8x because it needs one inference call instead of four.

isolated_nodes.name: Confidence matters for selective prediction
isolated_nodes.description: Selective classification rejects low-confidence examples, controlling the risk-coverage trade-off.

isolated_nodes.name: Sparsity found across models
isolated_nodes.description: Sparsity is also observed with Claude 3.7 Sonnet, with or without reasoning, and with an alternative 0-9 confidence range.

isolated_nodes.name: Logprobs unavailable in many APIs
isolated_nodes.description: Logit-based methods cannot be used with APIs that do not return logprobs (e.g. OpenAI, Claude, Bedrock), leaving only verbalization or sampling.

isolated_nodes.name: Scores highly but not fully correlated
isolated_nodes.description: Spearman correlation between verbalization logprobs and vanilla verbalization averages 0.89 across four datasets.

isolated_nodes.name: Digit independence is approximated
isolated_nodes.description: The expected-value computation treats tens and units digit distributions as independent, an approximation since standard APIs return logprobs only for generated tokens.

structural_reasoning: Sparsity observation drives both the evaluation critique (interpolation) and the proposed fix; results chain from metric correction to method comparison.
